body:
The session let the error field of a caused item in an acting answer show its text as written, cut at the text bound, on every answer carrier: the command line, the session socket, MCP and a kept check's kept answer.
The per-step capture now hides fields by its own answer set of eleven names (url, href, src, html, text, value, attrs, path, request, panic.payload, password); error left that set, which was the sink's twelve-name content set before.
The telemetry sink is unchanged: its twelve content names, error among them, still print [redacted] on its lines, and a failed fetch's error text appears 0 times on the sink's lines.
The caused result help served by help and as each acting MCP tool's description now says a field named error and every message cross as their author wrote them, such as a failed fetch's URL; the help kept its line count.
Measured: an app warn item reads error as its text with url and path redacted; on the tracing build the engine's Resource load failed item holds the failed fetch's error text while the sink line reads error=[redacted].
The widening was ratified by the founder's word; no span, log field, event, cause, exit, verb, carrier or dependency was added or retired.

body_fields.what: escher-telemetry's per-step capture behind the caused items of an answer, holding the answer's own hidden field set and the kept field value it judges by field name
escher's telemetry sink line format, the scrub by field name with its content-named set, applied to event lines and closed span lines
the driver's served help and acting MCP tool descriptions, including the caused result-field help naming which fields read [redacted]
the driver's caused items of an acting answer, each record's level, target, message and fields as captured during the step
the stand check that every acting failure answers its error text in caused, crossing MCP in process, the session socket and a kept check, and that no sentinel reaches the sink's lines

body: The scrub-set error item of escher-telemetry's scrub set: the sink still prints error=[redacted], but the capture now keeps error's text in a caused item, so a failed fetch's error text crosses the answer carriers as a field value.

The decision on scrubbing by field name in the sink and the capture: in the capture a content-named field no longer reads [redacted] by the sink's set; the capture judges by its own eleven-name answer set, error not among them.

The decision that answers echo nothing the caller typed: its exception for caused text scrubbed by field name now rests on the answer's own set, and error crosses as written, which can carry a URL the page or caller supplied.
The scrub-set url item: url stays [redacted] in both the sink and the caused item; a row that reads both sets as one set is now stale even where url's value holds.
Any row that holds the count of hidden names for the capture or the answer: twelve became eleven for the capture; the sink's twelve is unchanged.

Rows on Escher targets redacting the content-named set and on the reach of the scrubbing sink: true for the sink's lines, but a row that extends that rule to the caused items of an answer now has error as an exception.
The kept check file's answer and answer digest items: a kept answer's caused fields now hold error's text, so a check recorded with the old redacted value replays as a changed answer.
The escher-session help command and the help served as acting MCP tool descriptions: the caused field help text changed in content, same line count.

The failed-stylesheet error capture rows: a failed engine resource load now answers its error text, holding the fetch's URL, in the caused item's error field on the tracing build, while url itself stays redacted.

Rows on session logs carrying no page content and on engine log sites writing fixed messages: they hold for the sink's lines, but the answer now carries error text that can hold page-supplied content such as a URL.

body_fields.fact: The answer's caused items are judged by their own hidden set of eleven field names, apart from the sink's twelve-name content set; error is the one name the sink redacts and the answer shows as written, cut at the text bound, by the founder's ratified widening.

body: Span coverage rows: the command and tool_call spans, their fields, endings and the refusal cause names did not change; no span or span field was added.
Metric coverage and the absences of a metrics exporter, a telemetry backend or an error-reporting service: still absent.
Agent-run and cold-agent harness rows: their events, verdict fields, transcripts, artifacts and cleanup are not reached.
CI integration rows: workflows, artifact uploads, recording bounds and private directories are unchanged.
The sink's installation, target allowlist, RUST_LOG handling, output stream, resource keys service.name and service.version, panic hook and telemetry installed event are unchanged.
Script error surface rows, the window error event and window.onerror arguments, the script diagnostics drain and the WPT report are not reached.
escher-session exit codes, the host wire, the coverage role and refusal causes are unchanged; no cause, exit or carrier was added.

body_fields.reason: The chunk widens the acting verbs' caused item so its error field crosses as written (fct-tylyvsk5, fct-vk5mjci2), and it adds no interactive UI element and changes neither the a11y violation schema nor the obs log schema (a11y n/a, fct-jlhi4rif). The picked row contract/actions-answer/fields covers the actions verb's answer, which this chunk leaves unchanged (no verb, carrier or field added, fct-vk5mjci2), so the row stays true and a11y-plan owes nothing.

body_fields.value: caused carries an app's own messages and fields as their author wrote them, error included, scrubbed by the answer's own hidden field names, so an app that writes typed text into a record echoes it.
body_fields.because: The per-step capture now judges a caused field by the answer's own hidden set with error kept as written, so the exception's «scrubbed by field name» no longer names the set that scrubs and must say error crosses.

body_fields.promise: A caused item's fields are scrubbed by the answer's own set of eleven hidden field names, apart from the sink's twelve content names; a field named error crosses every answer carrier and a kept check as its author wrote it, cut at the capture's text bound, while the sink still prints it redacted.
body_fields.because: The chunk gave the answer its own hidden set of eleven names without error while the sink keeps its twelve, a promise at the answer boundary no standing row states.

body_fields.reason: The chunk changed only which field names a caused item's answer hides (error now crosses as written) and caused's result-field help text inside the same help line; every picked design-system row (one JSON line per command, help and MCP tool results as that line, no colour or ESC byte) still holds, no new UI element was rendered (Coverage tokens n/a, fct-jlhi4rif), and the task brings no new fact for this master (fct-tylyvsk5, fct-vk5mjci2, fct-lcn6twlz).

body_fields.promise: A caused item's field named error crosses every answer carrier (command line, session socket, MCP, a kept check) as its author wrote it, cut at the text bound, while url, href, src, html, text, value, attrs, path, request, panic.payload and password read [redacted].
body_fields.because: The per-step capture now judges caused fields by the answer's own eleven-name set without error, a ratified widening at the answer boundary that the surface's answer contracts do not yet state.

body_fields.value: Present only when the step caused something: an item per panic, error or record: kind, level, source, target, message cut at 1024 bytes, location, an error's boundary and chain, a log's fields, error kept, first reached handler; panics, then errors new since the boundary marks, then records; 16 kept
body_fields.because: The plan's expected amendment: a caused item's field named error now crosses as written, so «a log's scrubbed fields» must say the error field is kept.

body_fields.value: An `error` field is in the sink's scrub set, so the sink prints its value as `[redacted]`; the scoped capture keeps it in a caused item as written, cut at the text bound, so a failed fetch's error text crosses the answer carriers as a field value.
body_fields.because: The capture now judges a caused item's fields by the answer's own hidden set without `error`, so the row's claim that the capture keeps `error` as `[redacted]` and that the error text reaches no carrier is false.

body_fields.value: Scrubbing is by field name: in escher's own sink by the content-named set, a closed span's line judged pair by pair by the same rule, and in the scoped capture for every source by the answer's own hidden set; a scrubbed field reads [redacted], the message and other fields kept as written.
body_fields.because: The capture no longer reads the sink's content-named set but its own hidden set without `error`, so a content-named field no longer always reads [redacted] in a caused item.

body_fields.value: A caused item's message, chain and kept fields hold what their author wrote, a field of the answer's own hidden set reading [redacted] and an error field shown as written, cut at the text bound.
body_fields.because: A caused item's `error` field, content-named for the sink, now crosses as written, so the exception's «a content-named field's value reading [redacted]» no longer holds.

body_fields.name: The answer's own hidden field set
body_fields.rule: A caused item of an answer is judged by the answer's own hidden set of field names, apart from the sink's content-named set, a hidden field reading [redacted] on every answer carrier.
body_fields.except: A field named error, which the sink redacts, is shown in a caused item as written, cut at the text bound.
body_fields.because: The chunk splits the answer's hidden set from the sink's content set and lets `error` cross as written by a ratified widening, a decision no row of the PII section yet states.

body_fields.value: Each acting verb's answer carries caused on every ratified carrier when the step caused something: one item per panic, boundary error and kept record with its message, location, boundary, cause chain and fields, error as written within the text bound, every other content-named field redacted.
body_fields.because: The answer's capture now hides its own eleven field names and keeps a caused item's error field as written, cut at the text bound, while the sink still redacts error, so the row's «a content-named field read as redacted» no longer holds for error.

body_fields.value: A caused item's message and its error field hold what their author wrote; every other content-named field in it reads as redacted.
body_fields.because: A caused item's error field now crosses every answer carrier as written, so the exception must name it beside the message.

body_fields.value: An answer carries what the screen reads, ids, accessible names, control values with password and file input masked, snapshot text, diff, lint findings, UI graph, and an acting step's caused text scrubbed by the answer's own field names, error kept, never a NodeId or an attribute value as typed.
body_fields.because: The caused text is now scrubbed by the answer's own hidden field set, error not among it, rather than by the sink's content names the row implied.

body_fields.value: The sink's scrubbing reaches that sink only, escher's scoped capture hiding its own field set: upstream's fmt::init subscribers, env_logger and the panic hook stay unscrubbed.
body_fields.because: The scoped capture no longer reads the sink's content-named set but its own answer set, so the exception can no longer say one scrubbing reaches both.

body_fields.value: A reply never carries an attribute's text, but for what a caused item's message or error field holds as its author wrote it, such as a failed fetch's URL.
body_fields.because: The caused help now states that a field named error crosses as written and may hold a failed fetch's URL, so a reply can carry that text and the promise must name the exception.

body_fields.value: The stand load page's boot, with its self-answering LoadNet stand-in answering one fixed sheet after a delay, and the error-text check's failing page, whose FailingNet stand-in fails its fetch.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds a stand boot holding a failing network stand-in, so a load page is no longer the one stand boot that keeps a network provider.

body_fields.value: The stand load page's checks rely on its stand-in network answering the fixed URL with fixed bytes after a fixed delay, every other stand boot having no network provider but the error-text check's failing page, whose stand-in fails its fetch.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds a second stand boot with a network stand-in, so «every other stand boot having no network provider» no longer holds as written.

body:
In a caused item of an acting answer, a field named error now crosses as its author wrote it, cut at the text bound, on every answer carrier: command line, session socket call, MCP, and a kept check's kept answer.
The per-step capture now judges fields by the answer's own hidden set of eleven names (url, href, src, html, text, value, attrs, path, request, panic.payload, password); error left that set, so the capture's hidden names went from twelve to eleven.
The sink's content-named set (twelve names, error among them) and its stderr lines are unchanged: the sink still prints error=[redacted] and the error text appears 0 times on its lines.
The widening rests on the founder's own word, relayed (inputs I1): a failed fetch's error text, which can hold its URL, now crosses the answer while the url field stays [redacted].
The caused result-field help served by help and as each acting MCP tool's description now says error and every message cross as written; no verb, argument, cause, exit, carrier, endpoint, env var, span or log field was added, and no dependency moved.

body_fields.what: the scoped per-step capture that builds each caused item's fields for the answer, now holding the answer's own hidden field set apart from the sink's content names; its doc comments edited after implement to name that set as code text
escher's allowlist stderr telemetry sink, its content-named field set (twelve names) and the redaction of content-named fields on escher_ targets; edited by one line, its rule unchanged
the closed driver verb schema and its help text, served by help and as each acting MCP tool's description; the caused result-field help edited
the caused items an acting verb's answer carries (what failed, where, from which source, with its fields); doc text edited

the stand check that caused error text crosses the command line, MCP in process, the session socket and a kept check, and that no sentinel or raw href reaches the sink's lines, including a failed fetch on the tracing build

body: Caused text crossing: a content-named field no longer always reads [redacted] in a caused item; error crosses as written, holding what its author wrote such as a failed fetch's URL, a boundary widening ratified on the founder's word.
Value mask holds on every carrier: its exception that caused text is scrubbed by field name now means the answer's own eleven-name set, error not among them.
Session socket carries what the screen reads: its claim that caused text is scrubbed by field name is stale in its set; the socket now carries error text as written.

escher's allowlist telemetry sink: its exception or claim that the answer's capture shares the sink's content-name list is stale; the capture reads its own set, the sink's twelve names and lines unchanged.

Boundary widening rule: this session is a widening of what crosses an answer carrier (error text in caused), ratified by the founder's relayed word; a row that records ratified widenings gains this one.

MCP server help contract: the help text and each acting tool's description changed in the caused result-field lines (error no longer listed as reading [redacted]); byte-equal on both surfaces, line count unchanged.

Resource load failure log error and network tracing log error: the sink still prints error=[redacted], but the same record's error text now crosses the answer's caused item; a row saying that text never leaves the process is stale.
MCP result crossing and the session socket reply rows: a caused item in an MCP result or socket reply now holds error text as written, still bounded by the text cut and the result size bound.
Kept check rows (kept check keeps each answer whole, kept check call-content class, recorded check answer): a kept answer's caused item now holds error text as written, replayed and compared whole.

No echo of caller input, command line echoes nothing typed, session output holds no caller input: indirect, through the caused item; error text is what the app or engine author wrote, never caller-typed, but any row reading caused as fully scrubbed by content names needs its exception updated.

Escher targets scrub or withhold content-named fields and log sink redacts and allowlists: true for the sink still, but a row that extends that scrub to the caused answer now misstates it; the answer's set is eleven names.
Screen content stays out of logs: indirect; the sink keeps error redacted, the change widens only the answer, so the row holds unless it claims the answer and the log share one set.

body_fields.fact: Two scrub sets stand apart: the answer's capture hides eleven field names (url, href, src, html, text, value, attrs, path, request, panic.payload, password) in a caused item, while the stderr sink redacts twelve content names, error among them; error therefore reads [redacted] on sink lines and crosses the answer as written, cut at the text bound.

body: Authentication and authorization rows, and the CI token, publish and signing rows: no auth, CI workflow or release surface moved.
Dependency security rows: no dependency, pin, audit ignore or lockfile change.
Secret management and environment variable rows: no env var read or added, no secret touched.
Socket and MCP transport, bound, idle expiry, listener and request-grammar rows: no endpoint, port, verb, argument or request kind added; the sole listener and its bounds stand.
Error handling rows for refusal causes, refusal JSON, session errors, exit codes and MCP protocol errors: no cause, exit or error kind added or moved.
Input validation rows on select lists, ranges, stable element ids, accessibility names, password and file control masking: the control-value mask and the id rules are unchanged.
Data protection storage rows (history database, HTTP cache, cookies, TLS, clipboard, file dialog) and outbound request rows (per-host limits, schemes, GET-only fetches): none reached.
Command span and tool_call span contracts: no span or span field added; span lines unchanged.

The per-step capture behind an answer's caused items now hides fields by its own set of eleven names, the twelve content names less error, so a caused item's error field crosses every answer carrier (command line, socket call, MCP, a kept check's kept answer) as its author wrote it, cut at the text bound.
The sink's lines are unchanged: its twelve content names, error among them, still print [redacted], and a failed fetch's error text reads 0 times on the sink's lines.
The caused result-field help served by help and as each acting MCP tool's description was rewritten, six lines replacing six, error no longer among the names that read [redacted].
The error-text stand check grew from 7 to 8 tests (2 ignored): an app parse-warn step and an engine failed-fetch case on the tracing build, the carrier cases and the kept check's calls extended to it; the telemetry lib tests 25 to 26.
CI read red once at the Documentation job (a public doc comment linking a crate-private item), reproduced on the host by the doc leg and fixed; the local gate block had run no doc leg, as the plan listed none.
No verb, argument, cause, exit, carrier, log field, span, target or crate was added or retired.

edited — the telemetry sink's line formatter, its event rule and span-field store reading the content-field names that print [redacted]

body: A row holding that a caused item or an acting answer reads every content-named field as [redacted], or echoes no typed or logged text, now has error as its exception: error crosses as written, possibly holding a failed fetch's URL; the other eleven names still read [redacted].

decision/engine-items-asserted-on-tracing-build: a new engine caused-item case (a failed fetch's error text in the engine's error field) is asserted only on the tracing build, the package-alone build reading no engine item.
decision/mcp-result-decoded-whole: the MCP-in-process caused comparison now also compares the parse-warn item's error text.

contract/driver-session/act, contract/session-run/changed-node-states, contract/driver-session/run-carriers: the caused field of an acting call result now carries error text as written on every carrier.

contract/mcp-server/help, contract/mcp-help/parity, contract/cli-help/output, contract/escher-session-command-line/help, contract/mcp-server/tools-list, contract/mcp-tools-list/order, contract/tool-call-span/help: the help text and the acting tools' descriptions changed in content (same line count); help and the tool listing still the same bytes on both surfaces.

decision/stand-checks-in-both-layout-modes, decision/layout-tests-in-both-layout-modes: the parse-warn and failed-fetch cases run in both layout modes.
